meta.description: CAET Training Quick Reference Data - Comprehensive Entry Level Reference

dc.name: Ohm's Law (Voltage)
dc.description: Voltage equals current times resistance. Voltage is the electrical pressure that pushes current through a circuit.

dc.name: Ohm's Law (Current)
dc.description: Current equals voltage divided by resistance. Current is the flow of electrons measured in Amperes.

dc.name: Ohm's Law (Resistance)
dc.description: Resistance equals voltage divided by current. Resistance opposes current flow, measured in Ohms.

dc.name: Power (Basic)
dc.description: Power equals voltage times current. Measured in Watts (W). This is the rate of energy consumption.

dc.name: Power (Current Form)
dc.description: Power equals current squared times resistance. Use when you know I and R but not V.

dc.name: Power (Voltage Form)
dc.description: Power equals voltage squared divided by resistance. Use when you know V and R but not I.

dc.name: Electrical Energy
dc.description: Energy equals power times time. Measured in Watt-hours (Wh) or Joules (J). 1 Wh = 3600 J.

dc.name: Series Resistance
dc.description: Add all resistances in series. Current is the same through all components in series.

dc.name: Series Voltage
dc.description: Total voltage equals sum of all voltage drops. Voltages divide across series components.

dc.name: Voltage Divider
dc.description: Output voltage across R2 in a series circuit. Used to create reference voltages.

dc.name: Parallel Resistance (2 resistors)
dc.description: Product over sum for two parallel resistors. Quick method for calculating two resistors in parallel.

dc.name: Parallel Resistance (General)
dc.description: Reciprocal method for any number of parallel resistors. Total is always less than smallest resistor.

dc.name: Parallel Equal Resistors
dc.description: For n equal resistors in parallel, divide resistance by number of resistors.

dc.name: Current Divider
dc.description: Current through R1 when in parallel with R2. More current flows through smaller resistance.

dc.name: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL)
dc.description: Current entering a junction equals current leaving. Sum of currents at a node is zero.

dc.name: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL)
dc.description: Sum of voltage drops around a closed loop equals source voltage. Voltage rises = voltage drops.

dc.name: Conductance
dc.description: Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance. Measured in Siemens (S). Higher G = easier current flow.

dc.name: Wire Resistance
dc.description: Resistance of wire depends on resistivity (rho), length (L), and cross-sectional area (A).

dc.name: Short Circuit
dc.description: A short circuit has near-zero resistance, causing maximum current flow. Can be dangerous!

dc.name: Open Circuit
dc.description: An open circuit has infinite resistance, no current flows. Meter shows OL (overload).

ac.name: Inductive Reactance
ac.formula: X_L = 2 x pi x f x L
ac.description: Opposition to AC by an inductor. Increases with frequency. X_L in Ohms, f in Hz, L in Henrys.

ac.name: Capacitive Reactance
ac.formula: X_C = 1 / (2 x pi x f x C)
ac.description: Opposition to AC by a capacitor. Decreases with frequency. X_C in Ohms, f in Hz, C in Farads.

ac.name: Impedance (Series RL or RC)
ac.description: Total opposition to AC. Combines resistance and reactance. Measured in Ohms.

ac.name: Impedance (Series RLC)
ac.description: Series RLC impedance. X_L and X_C oppose each other, use net reactance.

ac.name: Ohm's Law for AC
ac.description: AC version of Ohm's Law using impedance (Z) instead of resistance.

ac.name: Frequency
ac.description: Frequency equals reciprocal of period. Measured in Hertz (Hz). Cycles per second.

ac.name: Period
ac.description: Time for one complete cycle. Measured in seconds. US power: T = 1/60 = 16.67ms.

ac.name: Wavelength
ac.description: Wavelength equals speed of light divided by frequency. Important for RF applications.

ac.name: RMS Voltage
ac.description: Effective AC voltage that produces same heating as DC. This is what meters read.

ac.name: Peak Voltage
ac.description: Maximum instantaneous voltage of sine wave. 120V RMS = 170V peak.

ac.name: Peak-to-Peak Voltage
ac.description: Total voltage swing from negative peak to positive peak. What you see on oscilloscope.

ac.name: Average Voltage (Full Wave)
ac.description: Average value of rectified AC. Used in DC power supply calculations.

ac.name: True Power (Real Power)
ac.formula: P = V x I x cos(theta)
ac.description: Actual power consumed. Measured in Watts (W). Only resistive loads consume true power.

ac.name: Reactive Power
ac.formula: Q = V x I x sin(theta)
ac.description: Power stored and returned by inductors/capacitors. Measured in VAR (Volt-Amps Reactive).

ac.name: Apparent Power
ac.description: Total power delivered. Measured in VA (Volt-Amps). S = sqrt(P² + Q²).

ac.name: Power Factor
ac.description: Ratio of true power to apparent power. PF of 1 is ideal (purely resistive).

ac.name: Resonant Frequency
ac.formula: f_r = 1 / (2 x pi x sqrt(L x C))
ac.description: Frequency where X_L = X_C. Circuit is purely resistive at resonance.

ac.name: Quality Factor (Q)
ac.description: Measure of circuit selectivity. Higher Q = sharper resonance, narrower bandwidth.

ac.name: Bandwidth
ac.description: Range of frequencies passed by a resonant circuit. Measured in Hz.

ac.name: Phase Angle
ac.description: Angle between voltage and current. Positive for inductive, negative for capacitive.

ac.name: ELI the ICE man
ac.formula: ELI: V leads I | ICE: I leads V
ac.description: Memory aid: In inductors (L), E (voltage) leads I. In capacitors (C), I leads E.

ac.name: RC Time Constant
ac.description: Time to charge/discharge to 63.2%. 5 tau = 99.3% charged. Tau in seconds.

ac.name: RL Time Constant
ac.description: Time for current to reach 63.2% of final value in RL circuit.

solid.name: Diode Symbol
solid.description: Arrow points direction of conventional current flow. Cathode has the bar (negative side).

solid.name: NPN Transistor
solid.description: NPN: Arrow Not Pointing iN. Most common BJT type. Current flows from collector to emitter.

solid.name: PNP Transistor
solid.description: PNP: Pointing iN Proudly. Current flows from emitter to collector (opposite of NPN).

solid.name: FET Terminals
solid.description: FET controlled by voltage on Gate. Current flows Drain to Source (N-channel).

solid.name: Diode Test (DMM)
solid.description: Good silicon diode reads 0.5-0.7V forward, OL (open) reverse. Shorted reads 0V both ways.

solid.name: Transistor Test (DMM)
solid.description: Test BJT like two diodes. Base to Emitter and Base to Collector should read 0.6V.

solid.name: Forward Voltage Drops
solid.description: Silicon diodes drop 0.7V, germanium drops 0.3V when forward biased.

solid.name: LED Voltage Drops
solid.description: LED forward voltage varies by color. Blue and white LEDs have highest drop.

solid.name: LED Current Limiting Resistor
solid.description: Calculate resistor to limit LED current. Typical LED current is 10-20mA.

solid.name: Zener Diode Operation
solid.description: Zener diodes regulate voltage by operating in reverse breakdown. Used for voltage references.

solid.name: BJT Current Gain (Beta)
solid.description: DC current gain. Collector current = Beta times Base current. Typical beta: 50-300.

solid.name: BJT Current Relationship
solid.description: Emitter current is sum of collector and base currents. I_E is largest current.

solid.name: BJT Saturation
solid.description: When fully ON (saturated), collector-emitter voltage is very low. Acts like closed switch.

solid.name: BJT Cutoff
solid.description: When OFF (cutoff), no collector current flows. All supply voltage across transistor.

solid.name: FET vs BJT
solid.formula: FET: Voltage controlled | BJT: Current controlled
solid.description: FETs have very high input impedance and are controlled by gate voltage, not current.

solid.name: Half-Wave Rectifier
solid.description: Uses one diode. Only half the AC cycle is used. High ripple, inefficient.

solid.name: Full-Wave Rectifier
solid.description: Uses bridge (4 diodes) or center-tap transformer. Both halves of AC cycle used.

solid.name: Filter Capacitor
solid.description: Larger capacitor = less ripple. Full-wave needs less capacitance than half-wave.

solid.name: Transistor Power Dissipation
solid.description: Power dissipated as heat. Must not exceed device rating. Use heatsink if needed.

solid.name: Op-Amp Inverting Gain
solid.description: Voltage gain of inverting op-amp. Negative sign indicates phase inversion.

solid.name: Op-Amp Non-Inverting Gain
solid.description: Voltage gain of non-inverting op-amp. Minimum gain is 1 (unity).

digital.name: AND Gate
digital.description: Output HIGH only when ALL inputs are HIGH. Like series switches.

digital.name: OR Gate
digital.description: Output HIGH when ANY input is HIGH. Like parallel switches.

digital.name: NOT Gate (Inverter)
digital.description: Output is opposite of input. Also called an inverter. Has only one input.

digital.name: NAND Gate
digital.description: AND then NOT. Universal gate - can build any logic function using only NANDs.

digital.name: NOR Gate
digital.description: OR then NOT. Also a universal gate. Can build any logic function.

digital.name: XOR Gate (Exclusive OR)
digital.description: Output HIGH when inputs are DIFFERENT. Used in comparators and adders.

digital.name: XNOR Gate (Exclusive NOR)
digital.description: Output HIGH when inputs are SAME. Also called equivalence gate.

digital.name: Buffer Gate
digital.description: Output equals input. Used for signal isolation, driving capacity, and delay.

digital.name: Binary Place Values
digital.description: Each position is a power of 2. Right to left: 2^0, 2^1, 2^2, 2^3, 2^4...

digital.name: Binary to Decimal
digital.description: Example: 1011 = 8+0+2+1 = 11 decimal. Read each 1 bit's place value and add.

digital.name: Decimal to Binary
digital.description: Divide by 2, write remainder. Repeat. Read remainders bottom to top.

digital.name: Hex Digits
digital.description: Hexadecimal uses 0-9 plus A-F (16 total values). Each hex digit = 4 binary bits.

digital.name: Hex to Binary
digital.description: Example: 0xA3 = 1010 0011. Convert each hex digit separately, then combine.

digital.name: Octal Number System
digital.description: Each octal digit = 3 binary bits. Example: Octal 7 = Binary 111.

digital.name: BCD (Binary Coded Decimal)
digital.description: Represents decimal digits 0-9 in 4-bit binary. Example: 25 = 0010 0101 BCD.

digital.name: DeMorgan's Theorem 1
digital.formula: NOT(A AND B) = (NOT A) OR (NOT B)
digital.description: Break the bar, change AND to OR. NAND equivalent.

digital.name: DeMorgan's Theorem 2
digital.formula: NOT(A OR B) = (NOT A) AND (NOT B)
digital.description: Break the bar, change OR to AND. NOR equivalent.

digital.name: Boolean AND Rules
digital.formula: A AND 0 = 0 | A AND 1 = A | A AND A = A
digital.description: ANDing with 0 gives 0 (masking). ANDing with 1 passes the value through.

digital.name: Boolean OR Rules
digital.formula: A OR 0 = A | A OR 1 = 1 | A OR A = A
digital.description: ORing with 0 passes through. ORing with 1 gives 1 (setting).

digital.name: Boolean NOT Rules
digital.formula: NOT(NOT A) = A | A AND (NOT A) = 0 | A OR (NOT A) = 1
digital.description: Double inversion cancels. Variable AND its complement = 0. Variable OR its complement = 1.

digital.name: SR Latch
digital.description: Basic memory element. S=1 sets output HIGH. R=1 resets output LOW.

digital.name: D Flip-Flop
digital.formula: Q follows D on clock edge
digital.description: Data flip-flop. Output Q copies input D on clock edge. Most common flip-flop.

digital.name: JK Flip-Flop
digital.description: Like SR but J=K=1 toggles output. No invalid state.

digital.name: Counter Modulus
digital.description: A counter with n flip-flops counts from 0 to 2^n - 1. Example: 4 FFs = mod-16.

digital.name: 555 Timer Astable Frequency
digital.description: Frequency of 555 timer in astable (oscillator) mode.

digital.name: 555 Timer Duty Cycle
digital.description: Duty cycle of 555 astable. Always > 50% with standard circuit.

digital.name: 7-Segment Display Types
digital.formula: Common Cathode: Logic HIGH lights | Common Anode: Logic LOW lights
digital.description: Common cathode: HIGH = ON. Common anode: LOW = ON. Check display type before wiring.

digital.name: ADC Resolution
digital.description: Resolution of n-bit ADC. 8-bit with 5V ref: 5V/256 = 19.5mV per step.

units.name: Nano (n)
units.description: One billionth. Example: 10 nF = 0.00000001 F. Common for capacitors.

units.name: Pico (p)
units.description: One trillionth. Example: 100 pF = 0.0000000001 F. Common for small capacitors.

units.name: Resistor Color Code
units.formula: Bk=0, Br=1, Rd=2, Or=3, Ye=4, Gr=5, Bl=6, Vi=7, Gy=8, Wh=9
units.description: First bands = digits, next = multiplier, last = tolerance. Bad Boys Race Our Young Girls But Violet Generally Wins.

units.name: Color Code Multipliers
units.formula: Bk=1, Br=10, Rd=100, Or=1k, Ye=10k, Gr=100k, Bl=1M

units.name: Resistor Tolerance Colors
units.description: Tolerance band (usually last). Gold (5%) is most common. Tighter tolerance costs more.

units.name: AWG Wire Gauge
units.formula: Lower AWG = Thicker wire = More current
units.description: American Wire Gauge. Common: 22 AWG for signals, 18-14 AWG for power, 10-12 for high current.

units.name: Decibels (Power)
units.description: Logarithmic ratio. +3dB = double power, -3dB = half power, +10dB = 10x power.

units.name: Decibels (Voltage)
units.description: For voltage ratios. +6dB = double voltage, +20dB = 10x voltage.

constants.name: Pi
constants.description: Used in AC reactance formulas (2 x pi x f). Also written as 3.14 for quick calculations.

constants.name: RMS Conversion Factor
constants.description: RMS = Peak x 0.707. Converts peak AC voltage to RMS (effective) value.

constants.name: Peak Conversion Factor
constants.description: Peak = RMS x 1.414. Converts RMS to peak value. 120V RMS = 170V peak.

constants.name: Average Conversion Factor
constants.description: Average = Peak x 0.637 (for full-wave rectified). Used in DC power supply calculations.

constants.name: Speed of Light
constants.description: Speed of light and electromagnetic waves. Used in wavelength calculations: lambda = c/f.

constants.name: Electron Charge
constants.description: Charge of single electron. 1 Amp = 6.24 x 10^18 electrons per second.

constants.name: US Line Voltage
constants.description: Standard US household power. 240V for large appliances. Peak voltage is 170V.

constants.name: TTL Logic Levels
constants.description: Standard 5V TTL levels. Inputs: LOW < 0.8V, HIGH > 2.0V. Outputs: LOW < 0.4V, HIGH > 2.4V.

constants.name: CMOS Logic Levels (5V)
constants.description: 5V CMOS logic levels. Wider noise margins than TTL. Also works with 3.3V and other supplies.

constants.name: Room Temperature
constants.description: Standard reference temperature for component specifications and calculations.
